steps: Knead the flour with a splash of warm water into a soft dough, then cover and rest it for 20 minutes.
Boil the potato until fork-tender, about 12 minutes, then peel and mash it roughly.
Mix the mashed potato with very finely minced onion, grated ginger, chopped serrano chile, chopped cilantro, a squeeze of lemon juice standing in for amchur, cumin, chili powder and salt.
Flatten a ball of dough in your palm, seal the potato filling inside it, and roll it out into a 6-inch round.
Griddle the stuffed paratha on a hot dry pan, smearing it with butter, until golden and blistered on both sides.
Fry the eggs in the remaining butter, season them with black pepper, and serve alongside the hot paratha with the last of the lemon to squeeze over.

note: Rebuilt as an actual stuffed paratha: Whole Wheat Tortilla 70g -> Flour 70g dough (kneaded with water in the step text; Water deliberately not added to ingredients). Filling gains Ginger, Cilantro, green chile (Serrano Chile) and Lemon as the amchur stand-in; Turmeric dropped, Chili Powder added; Onion cut 40->25g so the paratha does not tear. ~+80 cal, +2g protein.

steps: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces and marinate it in the greek yogurt with half the grated ginger and minced garlic, paprika, garam masala, cumin, coriander, turmeric and salt for at least 4 hours.
Cook the basmati rice according to package directions.
Spread the marinated chicken on a rack and broil or grill on high until the edges char, then set it aside.
Heat the olive oil and fry the diced onion until deep golden, then add the remaining ginger and garlic and cook for a minute.
Add the tomato sauce and the ground spices and cook until the sauce thickens and the oil separates.
Return the charred chicken to the sauce and simmer for 10 minutes, then stir in the evaporated milk off the heat.
Finish with chopped cilantro and serve over the basmati rice.

note: Relabeled British-Indian (Shish Mahal, Glasgow c.1971). Cauliflower 60g removed as macro padding; added Ginger, Garlic, Evaporated Milk (cream stand-in) and Cilantro. Chicken is now marinated 4h+ and charred before it meets the masala. Chili Powder -> Paprika as the Kashmiri chili stand-in. Kasuri Methi unavailable in the frozen vocabulary.

steps: Cook the basmati rice according to package directions.
Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 1 minute only, then drop it straight into ice water so it keeps its colour.
Blend the drained spinach with the garlic, ginger and serrano chile into a smooth green puree.
Melt the butter in a pan and bloom whole cumin seeds until they crackle, then add the diced onion and fry until golden.
Add the diced tomato, turmeric and coriander and cook until the tomato breaks down and the fat separates.
Stir in the spinach puree and simmer for only 5 minutes so it stays bright.
Add the cubed paneer, stir in the evaporated milk, and sprinkle the garam masala in at the very end off the heat. Finish with cilantro and serve over the rice.

note: Fixed the phantom cooking oil by adding Butter 10g (ghee stand-in). Added Ginger, fresh Tomato, Evaporated Milk (cream/malai stand-in) and Cilantro; Brown Rice 52g -> Basmati Rice 52g. Green chile via Serrano Chile, blended into the puree as Punjabi recipes do. Blanch cut to 1 min + ice bath; garam masala moved off the heat. ~+105 cal, mostly fat, as the report predicted. Kasuri Methi unavailable.

steps: Cook the basmati rice according to package directions.
Heat the olive oil and crackle whole cumin seeds, a bay leaf and a bruised cardamom pod in it.
Add the sliced onion and fry it to a deep golden brown, then add the minced garlic, grated ginger and chopped serrano chile.
Add the diced fresh tomato and the tomato sauce along with the turmeric, coriander, chili powder and garam masala, and fry until the mixture darkens and the oil separates from the masala.
Add the chickpeas with just enough water to cover them and simmer for 20 minutes, mashing a few against the side of the pan to thicken the gravy.
Take it off the heat and finish with a squeeze of lemon juice standing in for amchur and a handful of chopped cilantro. Serve with the rice.

note: Stripped the four ingredients that do not belong: Cauliflower 60g, Eggplant 60g, Paneer 50g and Red Lentils 13g. Chickpeas 65->85g; added Ginger, fresh Tomato 90g, Cilantro and Lemon (souring agent, standing in for amchur which is unavailable). Tomato Sauce cut 100->40g for body only; Brown Rice -> Basmati Rice. Whole-spice tempering and a bhuna step added. Protein drops ~9g as the report warned; calories -16%.

steps: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces and marinate them in the greek yogurt with the lemon juice, grated ginger, minced garlic, paprika, garam masala and salt for at least 4 hours.
Cook the basmati rice according to package directions.
Broil or grill the marinated chicken on high until the edges char, then set it aside.
Simmer the tomato sauce with the cumin, coriander and black pepper until it is thick and the fat begins to separate.
Whisk in the butter a piece at a time, then stir in the evaporated milk to make the makhani gravy.
Return the charred chicken to the gravy and simmer for 5 minutes, then finish with chopped cilantro and serve over the rice.

note: Restored the makhani method: yogurt moved out of the finished sauce into a 4h+ marinade with Lemon, the chicken is charred first, and the sauce is finished with Evaporated Milk (cream stand-in) rather than yogurt. Added Ginger, Garlic, Cilantro. Turmeric dropped; Chili Powder -> Paprika (Kashmiri stand-in). Onion stays absent, which is correct for the Moti Mahal original. Kasuri Methi unavailable. ~+55 cal.

steps: Cook the basmati rice according to package directions.
Peel and cube the potato and cut the cauliflower into florets.
Heat the olive oil and crackle whole cumin seeds in it, then add the grated ginger and chopped serrano chile.
Add the diced onion and fry until golden, then add the diced fresh tomato with the turmeric, coriander and chili powder and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the potato and cauliflower, toss to coat them in the masala, and cover for only 8 to 10 minutes until they soften.
Uncover and fry another 5 to 7 minutes, stirring rarely, so the edges brown and the sabzi cooks dry.
Take off the heat, sprinkle over the garam masala and chopped cilantro, and serve with the rice.

note: Kept it a dry Punjabi sabzi: Tomato Sauce 30g -> fresh Tomato 50g, the 20-minute covered steam replaced by 8-10 min covered then an uncovered browning fry. Added whole-cumin tempering, Ginger, green chile (Serrano Chile), Garam Masala off the heat and a Cilantro finish. Brown Rice -> Basmati Rice. Calories flat. Hing and Amchur unavailable.
